title: Project Pages Stopped Lying About What I'd Built | vitalii.no
description:
How a project page went from a static blurb I wrote once to a live snapshot of its real tech stack and newest work.

Clicking into one of my projects only ever showed a short, hand-written paragraph pulled from hardcoded translation files, plus a hand-picked 'highlights' grid. Neither reflected what the project's feature catalog actually looked like, or which technologies were really in use, as the project kept growing.

A new long_description column set was added to the projects table for all 13 projects. The project API route now fetches every published feature's tech stack and creation date, tallies the top technologies used, and keeps the newest ones with a title and short description per language — cached for 10 minutes. A shared component renders the tech-tag chips and the linked feature list on both the desktop and mobile project views, replacing the old static highlights grid entirely.

Every one of the 13 projects now shows a real write-up, up to 8 tech tags, and its 6 newest linked features instead of a static blurb — on both desktop and mobile, refreshed at most every 10 minutes.
